family.story: a poor family in Antananarivo, in an informal settlement, mother and father, 4 older siblings

milestones.question: wanjiru is six. school costs money the family barely has. do the parents send them?
milestones.reasoning: they wanted more for their child than they had
milestones.caption: 2032 · the first day of school. the family chose send them to school. the parents decided: they wanted more for their child than they had

milestones.question: you are seven. what do you do in the afternoons?

options.label: read and study with an older cousin
help the family earn: carry water, mind the stall
play outside with the street kids

milestones.reasoning: the family needed every hand
outcome: closer to the family, less time for school
milestones.caption: 2033 · afternoons after school. the family chose help the family earn. the parents decided: the family needed every hand

milestones.question: the family goes to worship every week. what do they raise wanjiru with?

options.label: raise them in the faith and its community

milestones.reasoning: it is how they were raised
outcome: grew up inside a faith community
milestones.caption: 2035 · the family faith. the family chose raise them in the faith and its community. the parents decided: it is how they were raised

milestones.question: you are twelve. the family needs money. do you stay in school?

options.label: leave school and work to feed the family
work in the day, study at night

milestones.reasoning: the family needed every hand
outcome: earned a little, school ended at twelve
milestones.caption: 2038 · stayed in school or left. the family chose leave school and work to feed the family. the parents decided: the family needed every hand

milestones.question: you are sixteen. friends pass around cigarettes and drink. what do you do?

options.label: say no and join a sports team

milestones.reasoning: i want to stay healthy and find friends who lift me up.
milestones.thought: i'll skip the smoke and join a team, feel stronger together.
outcome: found a team and a habit
milestones.caption: 2042 · cigarettes, drink, or sport. chose say no and join a sports team over say no and go home, because an earlier life learned: choose activities that strengthen your body and community instead of those that weaken the

milestones.question: you are 17, with 6 years of school, in Antananarivo. which path?

options.label: work the family farm or stall

milestones.reasoning: becoming a nurse lets me stay healthy while helping my neighbors, building trust and support.
milestones.thought: i want a job that keeps me strong and lets me give back to the people around me.
milestones.caption: 2044 · the path after school. chose train as a nurse over work the family farm or stall, because an earlier life learned: choose activities that strengthen your body and community instead of those that weaken them

milestones.question: you have a little free time. where does it go?

options.label: keep up with close friends, every week
join a community group (faith, sport, neighborhood)

milestones.reasoning: my close friends keep me grounded and give me strength for the tough days ahead
milestones.thought: i'll call marie tonight, we haven't talked in a while but i need that steady voice
milestones.caption: 2045 · who to spend time with. chose keep up with close friends over work extra shifts, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: training is done (nursing). which job?

options.label: nurse at a rural clinic that has none
sell cheap fake medicine on the side, it pays

milestones.reasoning: i want to use my training to help people in my own city where i already know the needs.
milestones.thought: i feel proud to finally work at the hospital and give back to my community.
milestones.caption: 2048 · the first real job. chose nurse at the city hospital, i want to use my training to help people in my own city where i already know the needs

milestones.question: you are 24. wages here are low. stay in Antananarivo or go?

options.label: migrate to Saudi Arabia for work

milestones.reasoning: i need more money for savings and better health services, so moving to saudi arabia makes sense.
milestones.thought: i've saved enough to take a risk, hoping a higher salary will give me security and access to good care.
milestones.caption: 2050 · move or stay. chose migrate to saudi arabia for work, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one

milestones.question: you met someone you like. what do you do?

options.label: wait, focus on yourself for now

milestones.reasoning: i need to make sure i can stand on my own feet before tying my future to someone else.
milestones.thought: i'll focus on building my savings and trust in myself first.
milestones.caption: 2052 · love. chose wait over commit, i need to make sure i can stand on my own feet before tying my future to someone else

milestones.question: you children?
milestones.reasoning: i need more stability and savings before bringing a child into this uncertain world.
milestones.thought: i'll focus on building a stronger foundation before expanding my family.
milestones.caption: 2054 · children. chose wait a few years over no children, i need more stability and savings before bringing a child into this uncertain world

milestones.question: you earn about $133 a month. what do you do with it?
milestones.reasoning: i need a cushion for future health costs and unexpected unrest.
milestones.thought: i'll set aside ten percent each month; it feels like a small step toward security.
milestones.caption: 2055 · what to do with money. chose save a tenth every month over enjoy it now, i need a cushion for future health costs and unexpected unrest

milestones.question: you are 31. your body is starting to complain.
milestones.reasoning: my body is already sending signals, i can't ignore them.
milestones.thought: i'll start walking each morning, feel the city wake up with me.
milestones.caption: 2057 · health at thirty. chose walk or train most days over no time for that, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one

milestones.question: you work as nurse. what next?

options.label: study at night for a better job
switch to work that helps people (care, teaching)
take a promotion that means cheating workers on pay

milestones.reasoning: i want work that lets me care for people directly and build supportive connections.
milestones.thought: i'll look for a role in community health teaching, where i can share and heal together.
milestones.caption: 2063 · mid-career. chose switch to work that helps people over start a business, because an earlier life learned: when grief strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: there is need all around you. do you give your time?

options.label: mentor young people in your trade

milestones.reasoning: i want my grief to help others and keep my spirit alive.
milestones.thought: i'll spend my evenings at the community center, sharing what i can.
milestones.caption: 2066 · helping others. chose volunteer every week over my family needs me first, because an earlier life learned: turn grief into service for those who are hurting

milestones.question: diagnosed with high blood pressure. what do you do?

options.label: follow the treatment, change how you live

milestones.reasoning: my health matters more than pride, i need to act before it gets worse.
milestones.thought: i will schedule a checkup and start the medication, then adjust my diet and exercise.
milestones.caption: 2067 · the diagnosis. chose follow the treatment over keep going as before, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one

milestones.question: chinedu died. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: turning my grief into service keeps me connected and gives purpose.
milestones.thought: i will volunteer at the bereavement group, sharing my pain to ease theirs.
milestones.caption: 2069 · grief. chose help others who lost someone over withdraw and work, because an earlier life learned: when grief strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: faith is everywhere here. where do you stand?

options.label: go deeper into faith and its community

milestones.reasoning: my community gives me strength and purpose, especially after loss.
milestones.thought: i feel the pull to join the prayer circle and help others carry their grief.
milestones.caption: 2069 · faith. chose go deeper into faith and its community over nothing changes, because an earlier life learned: when grief strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: wanjiru died. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: turning my grief into service honors those i lost and gives me purpose.
milestones.thought: i will volunteer at the community center, listening to others who mourn.
milestones.caption: 2071 · grief. chose help others who lost someone over withdraw and work, because an earlier life learned: when grief strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: you are 47. you have high blood pressure.
milestones.reasoning: my blood pressure won't wait, i need to catch problems early.
milestones.thought: i must schedule my next doctor visit; ignoring it feels reckless.
milestones.caption: 2073 · the checkup. chose regular checkups over ignore it, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and get checkups before small problems become big ones

milestones.question: a protest fills the streets of Antananarivo. do you join?

options.label: stay home, keep the family safe
help the injured at the edges
take what you can while the shops are open

milestones.reasoning: i want to stand with my community peacefully and show solidarity.
milestones.thought: i walked to the square, heart steady, hoping our voices bring change.
milestones.caption: 2077 · the protest. chose march over stay home, because an earlier life learned: when grief strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers
milestones.world: in Sub-Saharan Africa public approval collapses almost overnight: people now say out loud what they said in private

milestones.question: an old friend writes after years of silence.

options.label: write back, meet up, keep it going

milestones.reasoning: i miss the bond and want that trusted support as i age.
milestones.thought: i feel a tug in my chest, a quiet hope that old friendship can still lift me.
milestones.caption: 2077 · old friends. chose write back over too busy, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: chiamaka died, my mother. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: i turn my grief into service, it steadies my heart.
milestones.thought: i will reach out to others hurting and share the load, it feels right.
milestones.caption: 2079 · grief. chose help others who lost someone over withdraw and work, because an earlier life learned: when grief strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: you are 64, with $4324 saved. retire?

options.label: work part time, keep a purpose

milestones.reasoning: i need to stay active and keep some income while still caring for my health.
milestones.thought: i'll keep working a few hours a week, it gives me purpose and a little extra cash.
milestones.caption: 2090 · retirement. chose work part time over retire, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and get checkups before small problems become big ones

milestones.question: where do you want to grow old?

options.label: stay in the neighborhood, among friends

milestones.reasoning: i feel my community friends are my strongest support as i age.
milestones.thought: i will keep my weekly gatherings with the neighbors who have always been there.
milestones.caption: 2096 · where to grow old. chose stay in the neighborhood, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: what do you want to leave behind?

options.label: write down the family story for the grandchildren

milestones.reasoning: i want to keep helping others while i still can.
milestones.thought: i feel my days are still bright enough to give back.
milestones.caption: 2100 · what to leave behind. chose volunteer while the body allows over rest, because an earlier life learned: when grief strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: you are eighty. the walking group meets every morning.
milestones.reasoning: my body feels better when i move with others each morning.
milestones.thought: i join the walkers; the fresh air lifts my spirit and keeps my blood pressure steady.
milestones.caption: 2106 · staying active. chose join the walking group over stay home, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and get checkups before small problems become big ones

laws.title: World Research and Lunar Program Act
laws.text: Funds universities, research laboratories and a civilian lunar program open to every region.

laws.title: Universal Food Security Program
laws.text: Food aid and farm subsidies for regions with low food supply, paid from the world budget.

laws.title: Grid Expansion Act
laws.text: Builds solar, wind and grid capacity where electricity demand is not met.

lessonsLeft.choice: say no to cigarettes and drink and join a sports team
lessonsLeft.ledTo: found a supportive team, built regular physical activity, avoided early health problems, and created a circle of peers who encouraged healthy choices
lessonsLeft.rule: choose activities that strengthen your body and community instead of those that weaken them

lessonsLeft.choice: save a tenth of every month's earnings
lessonsLeft.ledTo: accumulated a modest safety net that later covered medical costs, allowed part‑time work in later years, and reduced stress during periods of unrest
lessonsLeft.rule: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

lessonsLeft.choice: volunteer regularly and turn personal grief into service for others
lessonsLeft.ledTo: built deep community ties, found purpose after loss, and created a network of mutual support that helped during later hardships
lessonsLeft.rule: when grief or hardship strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers
